newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish central bank launches new 100 punt note.
newsitem.headline: Irish central bank launches new 100 punt note.

text.p: The Central Bank of Ireland launched a new 100 punt note on Friday, possibly the last Irish banknote to be issued if Ireland succeeds in qualifying for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"If European integration moves ahead according to plan, this will be the last Irish banknote to be issued," central bank governor Maurice O'Connell said at the launch.
"The timetable for economic and monetary union provides that the Euro banknotes will be in circulation by the beginning of the year 2002."
O'Connell said the changeover would be a huge logistical exercise and Ireland was preparing for it on the assumption that it would participate in a single currency.
The 100 punt note features Charles Stewart Parnell, one of the great political figures of nineteenth century Ireland.
It is the fifth and final note in a series which has seen the security features of Irish banknotes substantially upgraded and the size of the notes reduced for greater convenience.
